Summer Research Project · Quantitative Investing

Reproducing and
Modernizing the
PB–ROE Strategy

From a 2011 stock-selection rule to a modern, point-in-time factor portfolio

10-minute research presentation · CSI 300 · Audited point-in-time workflow

Good morning. Our project rebuilds a Chinese PB–ROE rule published in 2011 as a modern point-in-time research process. We reproduce the historical rule, diagnose modern PB–ROE, redesign a compact eight-factor pool, require every extension to prove incremental information beyond that baseline, compare five-factor equal weight with Elastic Net and LightGBM, and build constrained portfolios. The historical rule is broadly reproducible. The revised factor mix improves risk-adjusted performance but not absolute return, and machine learning does not improve the final portfolio.

01 · Economic and market logic

Pay less for profitable firms—but define how the idea can fail

Economic mechanism

High ROE + Low PB → high PB–ROE score
  • ROE proxies the profitability of book capital.
  • PB is the market price paid for that capital.
  • Slow repricing can arise from anchoring, extrapolation and limits to arbitrage.

What would support it?

  • Positive and stable Rank IC and ICIR.
  • Ordered five-group forward returns.
  • Positive long–short payoff after costs.
  • Persistence in a frozen future period.

The project tests each condition separately.

Failure scenarios and limits

  • Low PB may signal a value trap; ROE can be cyclical or accounting-driven.
  • Crowding, regime change and turnover can erase the premium.
  • Free-data fields cannot replicate every Wind snapshot.
  • Static industry labels cannot be used causally through history.
PB–ROE is a value-quality hypothesis. ROE measures the profitability earned on book capital, while PB measures the price paid for that capital. If investors extrapolate recent weakness or arbitrage is limited, profitable but cheaply valued firms may be repriced slowly. This mechanism can fail: low PB can be a value trap, ROE can be cyclical or accounting-driven, the trade can become crowded, and costs can absorb the spread. We therefore require positive IC, ICIR, ordered group returns, post-cost payoff and frozen-period persistence rather than accepting an attractive cumulative curve.

The project is an executable cross-sectional research environment, not a spreadsheet backtest. Five canonical Parquet tables feed a point-in-time monthly panel. Eight independent factors are winsorized at one and ninety-nine percent and standardized within each month. The same panel supports IC, quantile tests, incremental screening, walk-forward models and a constrained CVXPY portfolio. AI assisted specification review, implementation, debugging and documentation. We retained responsibility for the research choices and conclusions. Ninety automated tests and thirty-one release audits independently verify the result.

03 · Time design

Separate windows prevent data mixing and future information

Historical test2005–2011

18 original-paper holding periods. This is the only window used for historical reproduction.

Warm-up2010–Apr 2012

Price history for momentum, volatility and covariance. It is input history, not a missing backtest.

Modern researchMay 2012–2022

Modern PB–ROE evaluation begins in 2012. Factor selection and model development use 2015–2022.

Evidence split2023–2025

Prior OOS for strict reversal; exploratory history for the revised 5-input models.

SignalMonth-end close
InformationEffective date ≤ signal date
TradeNext trading-day open
LabelUsable only after its exit date
The original reproduction is separate and contains eighteen real holding periods from 2005 to 2011. In the modern line, 2010 to April 2012 supplies trailing prices for momentum, volatility and covariance; it is input history, not a missing backtest. Modern PB–ROE evaluation starts in May 2012. Standalone gates and PB–ROE incremental screening use 2015 through 2022. Strict reversal was fixed before the 2023 to 2025 test, but the revised factor design was created after that period had been inspected, so the same dates are exploratory for the revised models. Every fold still excludes unfinished labels.

04 · Original-paper reproduction

The historical PB–ROE effect is directionally reproducible

29.86%

Reproduced PB–ROE Top 50 return, after the original cost assumptions.

35.00%

Original-paper result for the same core rule.

12 / 18

Holding periods in which the reproduced strategy beat its benchmark.

Not a field-by-field Wind replication. Free data, industry versions and execution details explain part of the gap.

The original score rewards high ROE and low PB. Using historical CSI 300 constituents and only information available at each signal date, the Top 50 portfolio earns 29.86 percent annualized after the paper’s cost assumptions, versus 35 percent in the report, and beats the proxy benchmark in twelve of eighteen periods. The direction and magnitude are reproducible. The industry-equal-weight version is not the best in our data, so this is not a field-by-field Wind replication.

05 · Modern re-evaluation

PB–ROE still predicts returns, but the economic payoff is much weaker

5.13%

PB–ROE mean Rank IC; ICIR = 0.82 and Newey–West t = 3.73.

2.78%

Raw PB–ROE annualized long–short return after 30 bp cost.

0.70

Five-group monotonicity—below the 0.80 selection gate.

Static industry labels are descriptive only; they are excluded from the formal historical target and constraints.

In the modern monthly sample, PB–ROE has a mean Rank IC of 5.13 percent, an annualized ICIR of 0.82 and a Newey–West t-statistic of 3.73. But the return after thirty basis points is only 2.78 percent annualized and five-group monotonicity is 0.70, below our selection gate. ROE alone has little economic payoff. The signal survives statistically, while its tradable payoff is much weaker than in the historical paper.

Why it may work

Main limitation

We test eight independent candidates in four economic groups: value, quality and growth, market behavior, and risk. The five rules were fixed before testing: predictive strength, statistical confidence, year-to-year consistency, ordered five-group returns and a positive spread after thirty basis points. Only one-month reversal passes all five in development, with IC 4.47 percent and a 5.92 percent after-cost return. Its later IC falls to minus 1.89 percent, so we preserve that failure. Standalone failure does not mean a factor is useful in combination; the next slide tests incremental value beyond PB–ROE.

07 · From PB–ROE diagnosis to factor extensions

Three of six extensions add information beyond PB–ROE

3 / 6

Momentum, reversal and low volatility pass every incremental gate.

5

Final inputs: core BP and ROE plus three incremental extensions.

−1.89%

Strict reversal still fails its prior-OOS standalone test.

Financial additions were not forced in.
EP, OCF/P and revenue growth fail the Add-one test.

This slide connects the PB–ROE diagnosis to the modern extension. BP and ROE are the core. For each of six extensions, we regress it on BP and ROE each month and test residual IC. We then add one-third of the candidate to two-thirds PB–ROE and require a positive IC improvement in at least half of development years. Momentum, reversal and low total volatility pass. EP, operating cash flow to price and revenue growth do not improve Add-one IC, so they remain documented candidates but do not enter the model. The final manifest has five inputs.

08 · Strict walk-forward comparison

Walk forward without leakage—and label evidence honestly

Evidence status
Prior OOS for strict reversal; exploratory for the revised models.

Inside each fold
Use 60 mature months; LightGBM fits 48 and validates on 12.

Monthly roll
The newest unfinished label is excluded, then the window moves one month.

Exploratory IC
PB–ROE 7.22%; 5-factor EW 8.35%; Elastic Net 8.86%; LightGBM 8.42%.

Each fold uses at most sixty mature months and rolls one month forward. LightGBM fits the earlier forty-eight and validates on the final twelve in time order; Elastic Net uses the full mature window. Models train on each month's centered return rank, which matches the Rank IC objective, while portfolios still use realized returns. In exploratory history, PB–ROE IC is 7.22 percent, five-factor equal weight is 8.35 percent, Elastic Net is 8.86 percent and LightGBM is 8.42 percent. The linear model ranks best, while the tree still does not beat it.

09 · Constrained portfolio

Simple factor diversification delivered the best risk-adjusted result

0.61

5-factor equal-weight Sharpe after 30 bp—the highest tested.

11.44%

5-factor equal-weight annualized return after 30 bp.

11.56%

PB–ROE baseline annualized return after 30 bp.

7.78%

Elastic Net; LightGBM earns 6.95% versus a 5.58% proxy benchmark.

We send PB–ROE, five-factor equal weight, Elastic Net and LightGBM through the same fully invested, long-only optimizer. After thirty basis points, the proxy benchmark earns 5.58 percent, PB–ROE earns 11.56 percent and five-factor equal weight earns 11.44 percent. The simple combination does not beat PB–ROE on raw return, but its Sharpe is higher at 0.61 versus 0.51 and its maximum drawdown is slightly smaller at minus 12.14 percent. Elastic Net earns 7.78 percent and LightGBM 6.95 percent. Higher Rank IC did not fully translate into portfolio return.

10 · Conclusion

What the study proves—and what it does not

Supported by the evidence

  • The historical PB–ROE direction and return magnitude are broadly reproducible.
  • PB–ROE retains modern ranking information, although its economic payoff has weakened.
  • The corrected first-announcement timing passes a hard lag audit.
  • No return label enters model training before its holding period has ended.

Not established

  • The original paper is not reproduced field by field.
  • The development-selected reversal signal does not persist after 2022.
  • Elastic Net and LightGBM do not beat the 5-factor equal-weight portfolio.
  • The revised positive result is not untouched out of sample.
The MVP result: diversify reliable weak signals; do not assume complexity is alpha.
To conclude, historical PB–ROE is broadly reproducible and retains modern ranking information. The standalone winner fails its prior out-of-sample test. A separate incremental audit retains three extensions beyond BP and ROE. Their five-factor equal-weight portfolio improves Sharpe and drawdown versus PB–ROE but not raw return. Elastic Net has the best exploratory Rank IC, yet neither model beats simple equal weight in the portfolio. The contribution is a point-in-time process that preserves negative evidence and tests whether complexity adds value. The decisive next step is truly new data after this code and manifest freeze. Thank you.
